quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. They may suddenly change direction without warning. Remember that children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: A train has passed you at a railroad crossing. What should you do next?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not proceed until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: You have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: In fog, you should use high beam headlights to see better.
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights instead. High beams will reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. How far back should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
Only one car length back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Keep extra distance so the truck driver knows you are there. Tailgating any vehicle removes your safety cushion if the driver stops suddenly.

questions.question: Oncoming headlights are blinding you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When blinded by oncoming headlights, look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: What turn is this bicyclist signaling?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand signals because they have no turn signals. A straight left arm means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles only

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is the blind spot around trucks and large vehicles where drivers cannot see. Avoid staying in these blind spots.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do with your headlights?

options.text: Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away.

questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when following another vehicle to avoid blinding the driver.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You might see this sign at intersections where U-turns are dangerous.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another car is coming toward you. What should your headlights be set to?

options.text: Either high or low beam is fine.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another car at night. High beams can blind other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that there is a steep hill ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign tell you?

options.text: The safe speed for a residential area.
The safe speed for leaving a highway.
The safe speed for entering a highway.
The safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed for leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safe speed for exiting a highway. In this example, the safe exit speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic coming from both directions, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right lane immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you must return to the right lane when you have enough space between your car and the other vehicle.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
When you might hit another vehicle.
When you are near a blind pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are near a blind pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may scare or confuse them. Slow down and wait until it is safe to pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead of the vehicle you passed. When you can see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to safely return to your lane.

questions.question: When may you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent do to your driving?

options.text: It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a serious crash.

questions.question: When you turn right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light (unless a sign says otherwise). When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone:

options.text: Construction workers must get out of your way.

questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected hazards. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means you:

options.text: Can turn in that direction after you slow down and check for traffic.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Can turn in that direction after you stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: The best way to prevent hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid when turning. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: After it rains for an hour or more.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Pavement is most slippery when rain first starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your tires are traveling on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when there is heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your tires from losing grip.

questions.question: You can lower the risk of hydroplaning by:

options.text: Using tires with the right air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires slide on a thin layer of water on the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: Traffic signs and road markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other cars are around.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and road markings control how traffic flows. They help drivers stay safe and reach their destinations. You must always obey traffic signs, signals, and road markings.

questions.question: You can help keep other drivers at a safe distance behind you by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.explanation: It is hard for drivers behind you to keep a safe distance. Help them by driving at a steady speed and signaling your turns, lane changes, and slowdowns early.

questions.question: A driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have finished crossing.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have finished crossing.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians may be crossing where you cannot see them. Stop your vehicle and only go when all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
They need the same amount of room to turn as passenger vehicles.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the rear. Do not stay in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than regular cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: Driving while distracted usually:

options.text: Makes the driver react more slowly to hazards.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the driver react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down how quickly a driver can respond to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: When is it permitted to drive if medication impairs your driving?

options.text: If you do not feel drowsy.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Using your cell phone to talk or text while driving does not increase your chances of crashing.
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving distracts you and increases your risk of a crash.
